날.x: Today is a really good day.
날.e: Marks special days: 생일날 (birthday), 어린이날 (Children's Day).
날.t: Useful phrases: 어느 날 'one day', 다음 날 'the next day'.

금요일.x: I watch a movie on Friday night.
금요일.e: 'Gold day' — named for Venus, the metal planet.
금요일.t: Pronounced [그묘일]. Slang 불금 ('fiery Friday') = a fun Friday night out.

잠.e: From 자다 (to sleep); 낮잠 = nap (낮 daytime).
잠.t: 잠을 자다 = to sleep; 잠이 오다 = to get sleepy; 잠이 안 와요 = I can't fall asleep.

맞다.m: to fit; to be right, to be correct
맞다.ex: 이 바지는 저한테 사이즈가 딱 맞아요.
맞다.e: Homonym warning: another 맞다 means 'to get hit', as in 비를 맞다 'get rained on'.
맞다.t: "맞아요!" means "That's right!" The dictionary form 맞다 is pronounced [맏따].

미술관.ex: 비가 오는 날에는 미술관에 가는 것을 좋아해요.
미술관.x: On rainy days, I like going to the art museum.
미술관.e: 미술 'fine art' + -관 = public building: 도서관, 박물관, 대사관.

떠들다.forms: 떠들어요 · 떠들었어요 · 떠들 거예요 · 떠드세요 (ㄹ drops)
떠들다.m: to make noise, to be loud, to chatter
떠들다.ex: 도서관에서 큰 소리로 떠들면 안 돼요.
떠들다.x: You must not talk loudly in the library.

목욕하다.m: to take a bath, to bathe
목욕하다.x: When I'm tired, I take a bath in warm water.
목욕하다.e: Literally 'wash the hair and bathe the body' — a full-body wash.
목욕하다.t: 목욕탕 is a Korean public bathhouse, a big part of traditional culture.

입장.x: Admission to the concert hall begins at 7 p.m.
입장.t: A different 입장 means 'position, standpoint' (제 입장에서는 = from my point of view).

입장.ex: 제 입장에서는 그 결정을 이해하기 어려워요.
입장.x: From my standpoint, that decision is hard to understand.
입장.e: Literally 'standing place': where you stand on an issue.
입장.t: A homonym 입장 means 'entrance, admission', as in 입장료 'admission fee'.

흔하다.ex: 김 씨는 한국에서 아주 흔한 성이에요.
흔하다.x: Kim is a very common family name in Korea.

둔하다.m: slow, dull; clumsy; insensitive, slow to notice
둔하다.ex: 저는 운동 신경이 둔해서 춤을 잘 못 춰요.
둔하다.x: I'm not very coordinated, so I can't dance well.

다루다.m: to handle, deal with; to cover (a topic)
다루다.ex: 이 책은 환경 문제를 자세히 다루고 있어요.
다루다.x: This book covers environmental issues in detail.

더하다.m: to add; to get worse, intensify
더하다.x: If the soup is bland, add a little salt.
더하다.t: In math, 더하기 is 'plus' and 빼기 is 'minus': 2 더하기 3은 5.

협동.x: In this game, teamwork with your friends is important.
협동.t: Pronounced [협똥]: ㄷ after ㅂ becomes tense.

체크인.t: As a verb: 체크인하다. Also used for flights at the airport.

도깨비.ex: 할머니가 도깨비가 나오는 옛날이야기를 해 주셨어요.
도깨비.x: My grandmother told me an old story with a dokkaebi in it.
도깨비.e: Native word of uncertain origin for a creature of Korean folklore.
도깨비.t: A 도깨비 is a mischievous trickster rather than an evil spirit: in tales it loves ssireum wrestling and carries a magic club (도깨비방망이) that conjures up gold.

빵빵.ex: 길이 막히자 차들이 빵빵 경적을 울렸어요.
빵빵.x: When traffic jammed, the cars started honking.
빵빵.e: 의성어 (sound word) imitating a car horn.
빵빵.t: Verb: 빵빵거리다 'to honk'. Casual 빵빵하다 means 'full, strong': 에어컨이 빵빵해요 'The AC is blasting'.

따돌림.m: ostracism, being left out, social exclusion
따돌림.ex: 그 학생은 반 친구들에게 따돌림을 당했어요.
따돌림.x: That student was ostracized by classmates.
따돌림.e: Noun from 따돌리다 'to leave someone out, shun'.
따돌림.t: Used with 당하다: 따돌림을 당하다 = to be ostracized.

철.ex: 철은 물에 오래 닿으면 녹이 슬어요.
철.x: Iron rusts if it touches water for a long time.
철.e: Homonym warning: native 철 means 'season', as in 제철 'in season'.
철.t: 철이 들다 is a different, native 철: it means 'to grow up, to mature'.

장맛비.x: The monsoon rain kept falling for a week.
장맛비.e: 장마 'rainy season' plus 비 'rain'; the added ㅅ makes 비 sound tense [삐].

열대야.m: tropical night (a night that stays above 25°C)
열대야.ex: 열대야 때문에 밤새 잠을 잘 못 잤어요.
열대야.x: I couldn't sleep well all night because of the tropical night.
열대야.e: Literally 'tropical-zone night'—a summer night that never cools down.
열대야.t: Pronounced [열때야] — ㄷ becomes tense after ㄹ in Sino-Korean words.

임대료.ex: 가게 임대료가 너무 올라서 장사가 힘들어요.
임대료.x: The store's rent went up so much that business is hard.

더구나.forms: A. 더구나 B (= what's more); ≈ 게다가
더구나.m: moreover, besides, what's more, on top of that
더구나.x: The weather was cold, and on top of that it even rained.

들어맞다.m: to fit, to match; to come true, to be right
들어맞다.x: Yesterday's weather forecast was exactly right.
들어맞다.e: 들다 'to go in' + 맞다 'to fit': fits right in.
들어맞다.t: Often about predictions: 예상이 들어맞다 'the prediction came true'.

손발이 맞다.forms: 손발이 맞아요 · 손발이 잘 맞았어요 · 손발이 안 맞다
손발이 맞다.m: to work well together, to be in sync
손발이 맞다.ex: 우리 팀은 손발이 잘 맞아서 일이 빨리 끝나요.
손발이 맞다.x: Our team works so well together that we finish quickly.
손발이 맞다.e: Literally 'the hands and feet match,' moving in sync.

궁합.m: compatibility (of a couple, by fortune-telling); good match
궁합.x: I had a fortune-teller check my compatibility with my boyfriend.
궁합.e: Traditionally read from a couple's birth dates; now also used jokingly for any good combination.

인플레이션.ex: 인플레이션 때문에 물가가 계속 오르고 있어요.
인플레이션.x: Prices keep going up because of inflation.
인플레이션.e: From English 'inflation'; often shortened to 인플레.
인플레이션.t: News often says 물가 상승 (rising prices) instead of the loanword in everyday contexts.

강박.x: He suffers from a compulsion to be perfect.

신소재.ex: 이 회사는 가볍고 튼튼한 신소재를 개발했습니다.
신소재.x: This company developed a light, strong new material.

문화권.ex: 한국과 일본은 같은 한자 문화권에 속해요.
문화권.x: Korea and Japan belong to the same Chinese-character cultural sphere.
문화권.e: 문화 = culture, plus -권 = zone or sphere: 문화권, 수도권, 영어권.

적대적.ex: 처음 만났을 때 그는 나에게 적대적인 태도를 보였어요.
적대적.x: When we first met, he was hostile toward me.

상대적으로.ex: 이 지역은 서울보다 집값이 상대적으로 싸요.
상대적으로.x: Housing in this area is relatively cheap compared to Seoul.
상대적으로.e: Literally 'facing each other' — measured against something else.

빈번히.x: Traffic accidents happen frequently on this road.
빈번히.t: Formal and written, common in news; in everyday speech use 자주.

동질성.ex: 두 지역 주민은 언어와 문화의 동질성을 가지고 있어요.
동질성.x: The people of the two regions share a common language and culture.

역사학.x: I majored in history in college.
역사학.e: Literally 'study of history'. -학 = field of study: 경제학, 심리학.

온실 효과.ex: 온실 효과 때문에 지구의 기온이 올라가고 있어요.
온실 효과.x: Because of the greenhouse effect, the earth's temperature is rising.
온실 효과.e: Literally 'warm-room effect' — the air traps heat like a greenhouse.

도화선.m: fuse; trigger, spark (that sets off an event)
도화선.x: That incident became the trigger for the protests.
도화선.e: Literally 'a line that leads fire', the fuse of a bomb.
도화선.t: Most often used as X의 도화선이 되다, 'to become the trigger of X', in news reports.

궁여지책.m: last resort, desperate measure (when out of options)
궁여지책.x: As a last resort, I borrowed money from a friend.
궁여지책.e: Literally 'a plan left over when cornered'.
궁여지책.t: Usually used as 궁여지책으로, 'as a last resort', at the start of a sentence.

조언자.ex: 그분은 제 인생의 가장 중요한 조언자예요.
조언자.x: That person is the most important advisor in my life.
조언자.e: Literally 'person of helping words'; -자 = person who does it: 과학자, 운전자.

배심제.x: The United States has run a jury system for a long time.
배심제.e: Literally 'system of those who sit in on the hearing'.
배심제.t: Korea has no full jury system; its version is 국민참여재판, where the jury's verdict is only advisory.

사기죄.ex: 그는 투자자들을 속인 사기죄로 징역형을 선고받았습니다.
사기죄.x: He was sentenced to prison for fraud after deceiving investors.
사기죄.e: -죄 = the crime of: 사기죄, 모욕죄, 절도죄.
사기죄.t: Pronounced [사기쬐]: 죄 is tensed after the noun, as in most -죄 crimes.

공정거래.x: The Fair Trade Commission investigated illegal practices by large corporations.
공정거래.e: 공정 'fair' + 거래 'trade, deal,' literally 'going and coming.'
공정거래.t: 공정거래위원회, Korea's antitrust agency, is usually called 공정위.

케인스주의.ex: 케인스주의는 불황기에 정부 지출을 늘려야 한다고 봅니다.
케인스주의.x: Keynesianism holds that government spending should increase during a recession.
케인스주의.e: From the economist John Maynard Keynes + -주의 '-ism.'

행정처분.x: He received an administrative sanction of a license suspension for drunk driving.
행정처분.e: Literally 'a government handling' of a case, such as a fine or license suspension.

용액.ex: 이 용액에 소금을 조금 더 넣어 보세요.
용액.x: Try adding a little more salt to this solution.
용액.t: This is only a chemical solution; a solution to a problem is 해결책.

나트륨.x: Ramyeon contains a lot of sodium.
나트륨.e: From German 'Natrium' (symbol Na) — that's why it isn't 'sodium'.
나트륨.t: Health news uses 나트륨 for dietary salt: 나트륨 섭취를 줄이세요 'cut down on sodium'.

유전공학.ex: 유전공학 기술로 병에 강한 작물을 만들 수 있어요.
유전공학.x: Genetic engineering can create crops that resist disease.

대번에.m: at once, right away, in one go
대번에.ex: 그는 내 목소리를 듣고 대번에 알아봤어요.
대번에.x: He recognized me at once when he heard my voice.
대번에.e: Usually with recognizing or succeeding verbs: 대번에 알아보다, 대번에 붙다.

통시적.ex: 통시적 연구는 언어의 변화 과정을 살펴봅니다.
통시적.x: Diachronic research examines how a language changes over time.
통시적.e: Literally 'through-time'; it follows change across history.

하룻강아지 범 무서운 줄 모른다.forms: 하룻강아지 범 무서운 줄 모른다더니 · 하룻강아지 범 무서운 줄 모르고
하룻강아지 범 무서운 줄 모른다.m: the inexperienced don't know what to fear; fools rush in (lit. a day-old puppy doesn't know to fear the tiger)
하룻강아지 범 무서운 줄 모른다.ex: 하룻강아지 범 무서운 줄 모른다더니, 신입 사원이 부장님한테 대들었어요.
하룻강아지 범 무서운 줄 모른다.x: Fools rush in, as they say: a new employee talked back to the department head.
하룻강아지 범 무서운 줄 모른다.e: 하룻강아지 is a newborn puppy (하루 'one day' + 강아지 'puppy'); it is too new to the world to know that a tiger (범) is dangerous.
하룻강아지 범 무서운 줄 모른다.t: Pronounced [하루깡아지]. Said of a newcomer who boldly takes on someone far stronger or more experienced, with a mix of disapproval and amusement. 범 is a native word for 호랑이.
nb: 미꾸라지 한 마리가 온 웅덩이를 흐려 놓는다
